sentence_stem: Had the manager read the report carefully,
correct_completion: she would have spotted the error.
full_sentence: Had the manager read the report carefully, she would have spotted the error.
acceptable_variants: she would have caught the mistake.
she might have noticed the mistake.

options.why_wrong: The stem sets up a hypothetical past condition, so the main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle, not a present tense.

options.text: she would have spotted the error.

options.why_wrong: 'Would spot' refers to the present. The inverted condition 'had read' refers to the past, so the result must also be in the past.
The present perfect states a completed fact, not the hypothetical result of a condition that did not happen.

explanation: In an inverted conditional, 'Had' plus the subject and past participle replaces 'If' plus the past perfect. The main clause therefore needs 'would have' plus a past participle. Polish speakers often use a simple conditional in both clauses, because Polish builds conditionals with a particle and a past form, so they tend to drop the perfect structure here.
translation: Gdyby kierownik przeczytał raport uważnie, zauważyłby błąd.
